title: Should AI-generated art be allowed in competitions?
description: The debate considers whether art competitions should permit entries created with generative AI, and under what disclosure or authorship rules.

facts.fact: The US Copyright Office recognises that works combining human-authored elements with AI-generated material can be copyrightable.
Human selection, arrangement or substantial modification of AI output can constitute protectable creative authorship.
In Adobe's 2024 survey of 2,541 creative professionals in eight countries, 83% said they already use generative AI tools in their work.
The US Copyright Office says prompts alone do not provide enough human control to make a user the author of AI output.
Copyright does not extend to purely AI-generated material or material with insufficient human control over expression.
AI-generated works can raise concerns about originality, consent and the use of artists' styles and training data.
